editorial:
Imagine having a rich dad who suddenly decides to give all his money away to the church. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow a retired doctor who has a sudden change of heart and starts spending his fortune on religious causes. Naturally, his children are not happy about losing their inheritance. They decide to take him to court to prove he is mentally unfit to handle his own cash. It is a classic family fight that feels like a stage play, focusing heavily on the tension between a father's faith and his kids' greed.

The acting is solid and keeps you interested even though there is not much action. You will find yourself rooting for the dad, though the movie does slow down a bit in the middle. If you like old-school courtroom dramas with a moral lesson, you will really enjoy this one. Since it is an older film, you might want to track down a 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture quality, or just rent it on Apple TV if you want a quick watch tonight.
endingExplained: In the end, the court case reveals the truth about the doctor's mental state. It turns out he is perfectly sane and making a conscious choice to help others. The family has to accept that they cannot force him to keep the money for them. The movie wraps up with a lesson on greed and faith, showing that the doctor found more peace in giving than his children found in wanting.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old movies about family conflicts and morality.
